chapter: Coming up in New York and Harlem theatres
title: Introducing Cootie Williams to Duke and Johnny Hodges in Boston
summary: At Small's, Whaley introduces Cootie Williams to Duke, and recalls first hearing a young Johnny Hodges in Boston.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: I used to have a band and one day Duke came in there and I called -- I said, go get this guy, what's his name, trumpet player. He was playing downtown at a dancing school and I --

Cootie Williams. He was living at 131st with Chick Webb and I said to the guy go by and tell Cootie to come on by here, so Cootie come by and Duke was in there and I introduced Cootie to Duke and Duke, you know, they got together after awhile.

Just like Johnny Hodges in Boston. Johnny Hodges, I used to have a job up there in the Avery Hotel, it's a little place in a alley and they had the hotel there, next to Boston Street and we used to go up there and one day this fellow he had short pants on, come up there and he says can I play and I said sure, come on up and play. Johnny Hodges.
He stayed with Duke's band for 30, 40 years.

He sure did. He was the greatest -- to me he was the greatest, he had more soul for a guy like him. He could do more on a sax. Billy Smith was the next guy I thought was great. Used to be with Jimmy Lunceford.
Willie Smith. Tell me about some of these other piano players, some of these guys. What about --
